response.answer: To detect realistic effect sizes for classification/segmentation, power calculations require sufficient specimens and repeats per damage mode, typically determined by desired significance level and statistical power. Generally, hundreds to thousands of samples are needed, depending on effect size and variability. Specific numbers depend on detailed statistical analysis.

results.content: Bias can arise due to a variety of sources: (i) errors from faulty logic or incorrect premises; (ii) nonrandom sample such as volunteers; (iii) small sample that fails to represent the entire spectrum of subjects; (iv) concomitant medication or concurrent disease that might seem unrelated; (v) lack of matching in case and control groups; (vi) unaccounted confounders; (vii) wrong or blurred definitions that give room to assessor to use subjective interpretations; (viii) errors in diagnostic or screening criteria; (ix) insufficient instructions regarding what to do in unusual or unforeseen situations so that observers use their own discretion that can vary from observer to observer; (x) more care in assessment of cases than controls; (xi) differential recall of past events by cases and controls; (xii) not being able to recall events of the past, or selective recall of serious events and not of mild events; (xiii) differential compliance of regimen and instructions by cases and controls; (xiv) suppression of information by patients because of stigma or otherwise; (xv) premeditated response by a group after consulting each other; (xvi) aberration in response due to unsuspecting event such as sudden illness or death in the family; (xviii)some control subjects or some subjects in treatment group getting unaccounted therapy outside the study; (xix)detection of some cases in early phase of the disease and some in the late phase; (xx)prevalent cases could be more of those who survive for longer duration, and thus may be of better health; (xxi)the study is based on hospital cases but the exposure is such that increases the chance of admission; results.content: This submission discusses the development of an intraoperative platform that provides real-time assessment of the resection bed with a two-stage process: a rapid-scanning optical coherence tomography (OCT) handheld probe and a high-resolution multiphoton (NLO) and optical coherence microscopy (OCM) imaging module affixed to a semi-autonomous medical robot arm. Virtual pathology enables real-time, histology-like imaging of fresh tissue, offering a non-destructive alternative to FFPE and frozen section analysis for identifying positive surgical margins. We present a fully integrated, mobile stimulated Raman scattering imaging system that enables real-time, label-free assessment of brain tumor tissue. This study presents a novel spatial augmentation system that integrates real-time fluorescence lifetime imaging (FLIm) with preoperative MRI navigation to enhance intraoperative guidance during brain tumor resection. The compact, energy-efficient sensor unit captures multimodal data—including intra-articular temperature, optical imaging, and light-scattering properties of synovial fluid—enabling real-time assessment of infection dynamics. We propose a multimodal imaging system that integrates optical coherence tomography (OCT), autofluorescence imaging (AFI), and photodynamic detection (PDD) to enable real-time monitoring of photodynamic therapy (PDT) in the oral cavity.
